meta.title: Ebanist — from measurements to cut list in 10 minutes
meta.desc: Furniture design app for cabinetmakers. Design a unit on your phone and get the cut list, part labels, assembly sheet and technical drawing. Runs in the browser, works offline. Free for 1 project.
meta.ogTitle: Ebanist — from measurements to cut list in 10 minutes
meta.ogDesc: Design a unit on your phone, on site. Get the 3D model, the cut list, the labels and the assembly sheet.
hero.sub: A furniture design app for cabinetmakers. It runs in the browser — nothing to install — and keeps working offline, on site.
hero.proof: 15 furniture types · Blum & Häfele · Egger decors · PDF output
hero.alt: Two-door wardrobe with walnut fronts, 1000 × 2200 × 600 mm, drawn by Ebanist
prob.h: Three things that cost a workshop every week.
prob.1: Cut lists added up by hand, at night.
prob.1s: Every part computed from one model — finished size, to 0.1 mm.
prob.2: A wrong depth discovered on site.
prob.2s: Thickness comes from the material. If the carcass doesn’t add up, the PDF doesn’t print.
prob.3: Days lost between the drawing and the factory.
prob.3s: Cut list, labels and assembly sheet leave the same model, the same day.
story.note: Wardrobe W1000 · real data from the app
story.a.d: Width, height, depth. The carcass, the divider, the shelves and the doors follow — every part derived in one place.
story.b.d: 30 parts, each with its role, axes and thickness. Nothing is placed by absolute coordinates: move a size and everything follows.
story.c.d: Finished sizes, edge banding, material. The table your saw operator reads, straight from the model.
story.d.d: 70 × 37 mm, 24 per A4 sheet. Size, material and which edges get banded, drawn on the label.
story.e.d: System 32 rows on the sides, five hinge cups per door at 100 · 579 · 1057 · 1536 · 2014 mm. The fitter reads it, doesn’t guess.
story.asm.sys: System 32 · Ø5 · 37 mm from the front edge

bento.h: Everything the workshop used to write by hand.
bento.types.d: All parametric. Change a size, every part follows.
bento.hw.d: Real part numbers, editable. Counted once — the quote and the assembly sheet always agree.
bento.mat.d: Thickness comes from the material, never from an “18” typed at random.
bento.lbl.d: Edge-banding diagram and cut-outs on every label.
bento.draw.d: Front and side views with the dimensions from the model.
bento.room.d: 3D render with real wood grain, rotate on three axes, export a JPG for WhatsApp.
bento.lab.d: JSON without prices for the cutting centre, plus CSV import and export.
bento.off.d: Projects stay on your device. Full backup in one file, whenever you want.

faq.q1: Do I need to install anything?
faq.a1: No. Ebanist opens in the browser and you can add it to your home screen so it opens like an app. The Android app is coming soon on Google Play.
faq.a2: Yes — in Safari on iPhone and iPad, as well as on Android phones, tablets and any PC.
faq.a3: On your device, in the browser’s storage. There is no account and nothing is uploaded. A full backup is one JSON file you can export at any time, for free.
faq.a4: Yes. After the first launch the whole app — survey, design, 3D, cut list — works without a network.
faq.a5: Any cutting service that reads a PDF or CSV cut list. The workshop package (JSON, no prices) carries every part with its edging. Native machine files (Biesse, SCM, Homag) are in development with a partner and not available yet.
faq.q6: Can I put my own logo on the PDFs?
faq.a6: Yes, with Pro: Settings → Logo on PDFs. Your company name and details go on every document.
